preamble: The voiced velar plosive /g/ surfaces as the labiodental fricative [v] in the Russian adjectival and pronominal genitive/accusative ending spelled -ого/-его and in the pronoun его 'him, his' and the adverb сегодня 'today'. The spelling preserves the older consonant while the standard pronunciation has [v]; the change is lexically and morphologically restricted rather than a general sound law, so the shift is rare cross-linguistically.

examples.note: Wiktionary respells the word as ево́; the declension note states that г in the genitive/accusative ending is pronounced /v/.
Genitive/accusative of кто 'who', with the same -ого ending.
The rule extends to every adjective ending in -ого/-его.

sources: Timberlake, A. (2004). A Reference Grammar of Russian. Cambridge University Press.
